title: model-loading-weights-shard-scratchpad-amelia-garcia
content:
Context:
- Reproducing intermittent failures when loading vetting-llama-30b checkpoint on dedicated cluster (nv4a-80gb nodes). Failure happens during final weight merge phase on rank0; other ranks exit with code 0 or hang depending on run.
- Reported in JIRA-INF-4321; initial triage suggests shard download or checkpoint format mismatch.

Symptoms observed (logs snippets):
- rank0 log (abridged):
  [2024-11-03 09:12:17,842] ERROR model_loader.py:412 - Failed to load checkpoint: EOFError: unexpected end of file while reading weights blob
  Traceback (most recent calls last):
    File "model_loader.py", line 384, in load_checkpoint
      weights = _read_shard(f)
    File "io_ops.py", line 210, in _read_shard
      data = f.read(expected_size)
  EOFError: expected 2147483648 bytes, got 1879048192

- s3 transfer logs show occasional 200 OK but truncated content-length reported by proxy. Example:
  2024-11-03T09:11:58Z GET /s3/v2/checkpoints/vetting-llama-30b/shard-0001-of-0008.bin 200 1800000000 bytes

- Another run shows different error: KeyError: 'shard-0005-of-0008' during manifest parse on rank3

Commands/troubleshooting tried (notes):
1) Verify checksum locally after download via aws cli:
   aws s3 cp s3://redwood-checkpoints/vetting-llama-30b/shard-0001-of-0008.bin ./ && sha256sum shard-0001-of-0008.bin
   -> observed different SHA for shard-0001 in one failed run vs manifest (manifest sha: a3f1.. vs local: a3f1.. same)  (inconsistent: sometimes matches, sometimes not)
2) Use curl through proxy to double-check Content-Length header:
   curl -I -L "https://s3-proxy.internal/redwood-checkpoints/vetting-llama-30b/shard-0001-of-0008.bin"
   -> Content-Length: 1879048192 (mismatch expected 2147483648)
3) Re-ran aws s3 cp with --no-verify-ssl and with --expected-size? (no such flag) - attempted streaming download with aws-v4 signer shim to avoid proxy chunking. No change.
4) Ran parity check across nodes:
   on node: ls -l shard-000*.bin -> sizes: [shard-0001: 1.75GB, shard-0002: 2.00GB, shard-0003: 2.00GB, ...]
5) Manually downloaded same shard from another region (us-west-2) and sizes matched expected -> suggests proxy/regional truncation.
6) Increased HTTP client timeout and retried downloads with ranged requests; ranged requests succeeded and returned full size when retried, but initial full-range request sometimes truncated.

Hypotheses:
- Upstream proxy (s3-proxy.internal) is truncating large objects intermittently due to connection resets or a bug when streaming >2GB objects. Evidence: Content-Length smaller on HEAD/GET via proxy; regional direct S3 OK.
- Checkpoint manifest may be inconsistent with uploaded shard sizes in a small number of uploads (partial upload succeeded). But manifest SHA mostly matches for affected shards, so less likely.
- Parallel download + merge logic in model_loader expects blocking reads; if a partial read isn't detected properly (missing validation), EOFError surfaces later.
- Some ranks see missing shard entries due to eventual consistency on manifest listing (KeyError on shard-0005) — possible race between manifest update and object promotion.

Immediate mitigation tried:
- Added explicit range-based download fallback: if full GET returns size < expected, try ranged GET 0-(expected-1). This recovered a few runs.
- Retry loop with exponential backoff for downloads and verify size + sha256 before exposing to loader.
- For dogfood cluster, temporarily set loader to fail fast and surface which shard failed to force restarts (helps get fresh downloads).

Proposed long-term fixes:
1) Improve uploader pipeline to atomically write shards + manifest (upload to temp prefix then move/rename or use manifest revisioning).
2) Harden proxy (s3-proxy) to support large streaming objects and increase max chunk size; add integration tests for >2GB objects.
3) Model loader: always verify shard size and sha256 before attempting to memory-map or merge; treat partial downloads as transient and retry.
4) Add checksum/etag verification in serving runtime fetch path and surface clear error messages (e.g., "shard size mismatch: expected X, got Y").
5) Add manifest consistency checks: ensure manifest lists all expected shards and reachable object HEADs before starting distributed load.

Notes for root cause timeline (best effort):
- 2024-11-02: uploader job retried due to transient s3 5xx; may have left a partial object in proxy cache.
- 2024-11-03: first customer-facing incident, model failed to warm and fallback triggered.
- 2024-11-03 09:30: observed truncated Content-Length via proxy logs; engineering oncall alerted.

Reproduction steps (local cluster):
1) Use test checkpoint with one shard intentionally truncated (truncate binary file by 256MB).
2) Start serving runtime with loader verbose logging: 
   export LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG
   ./serve --model-path s3://redwood-checkpoints/vetting-llama-30b-test
3) Observe loader behavior: should detect truncated size and throw EOFError as above.

Temporary workarounds for customer-facing clusters:
- Add prefetch validation job before rolling model to cluster: head each shard, download small sample bytes, verify content-length, and compute sha256 for small objects or use S3 ETag for multipart awareness.
- Disable reuse of proxy cache for ranges >1GB until proxy patch is deployed.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is the proxy performing multipart assembly incorrectly? Need proxy team to review logs for object PUTs around 2024-11-02.
- Should we change default upload tool to always use multipart with explicit part-size 256MB? (tradeoffs: overhead vs reliability)
- Consider exposing a small pre-warm step in API to validate checkpoint integrity before serving speed-sensitive traffic.

Notes to self (debug checklist):
- [ ] Collect full s3-proxy logs for 2024-11-01..2024-11-04 (request ids: x-req-9912, x-req-9920)
- [ ] Add shard size + sha256 verification to model_loader (PR skeleton started in local branch amelia/shard-verify)
- [ ] Sync with infra/proxy team in standup (cc: Jordan, Maya)
- [ ] Draft postmortem outline once RCA confirmed

Quick snippets (commands used):
- aws CLI download + sha256:
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-checkpoints/vetting-llama-30b/shard-0001-of-0008.bin ./ && sha256sum shard-0001-of-0008.bin
- curl HEAD via proxy:
  curl -I -L "https://s3-proxy.internal/redwood-checkpoints/vetting-llama-30b/shard-0001-of-0008.bin"
- ranged curl to reassemble:
  curl -r 0-2147483647 -o shard-0001.bin "https://s3-proxy.internal/.../shard-0001-of-0008.bin"

If anything else comes up I'll append logs here. For now leaning on proxy truncation as primary cause.

-- Amelia G.
